title: Polynomial generators for an affine etale chart algebra
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Regard $X$ as an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ through $X\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with the same etale scheme charts and small etale ringed site. Let $V$ be an affine scheme and $f:X\to V$ an absolute morphism, that is, a morphism of algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, whose diagonal is a closed immersion on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\varphi:U\to X$ be representable surjective etale with $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ affine. Use small-etale module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Then $\varphi_*\mathcal O_U$ is quasi-coherent and there are $m\ge0$ and elements $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in B=\Gamma(X,\varphi_*\mathcal O_U)$ such that the evaluation map of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $$e:\mathcal O_X[z_1,\ldots,z_m]\longrightarrow\varphi_*\mathcal O_U,\qquad z_i\longmapsto g_i,$$ is surjective, and its kernel as a module sheaf is quasi-coherent. Here the polynomial sheaf is the free commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra on $m$ global indeterminates; as a module it is the coproduct of one copy of $\mathcal O_X$ for each monomial. No cohomology vanishing or finite-type hypothesis on $X$ or $V$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U; kernel from spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent). Change of base scheme: spaces.tex Tag 04SG (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme).

proof.text: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ as stipulated in the statement, so the separated morphism $f$ and all its charts have a common base. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Apply [lem-trf-space-separated-affine-chart-overlap] to the two copies $U_0,U_1$ of $U$: $R=U_0\times_XU_1$ is an affine scheme, its projections $p_i$ are etale, and $j:R\to U_0\times_VU_1$ is a closed immersion. Put $C=\Gamma(R,\mathcal O_R)$, and let $t,s:B\to C$ be induced by $p_0,p_1$, respectively. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the target of $j$ has ring $B\otimes_A B$, with the two factor maps specified there. The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore gives a surjection $q:B\otimes_A B\twoheadrightarrow C$, $q(b\otimes b\prime)=t(b)s(b\prime)$.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof, from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U.

proof.text: The map $p_0:R\to U_0$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], since both schemes are affine. It is the base change of $\varphi$ along the surjective etale chart $U_0\to X$. Thus [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] makes $\varphi$ affine, hence quasi-compact and separated. The module $\mathcal O_U$ is quasi-coherent by its one-generator free presentation in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward] to $\varphi$ and $\mathcal O_U$: $\mathcal F=\varphi_*\mathcal O_U$ is quasi-coherent. This uses no finiteness property of $f$ or of $X\to V$.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof, from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], clause (1), to the etale affine scheme map $p_0:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ from step 1. Hence $C$ is a finitely presented, in particular finitely generated, algebra via $t:B\to C$. Choose finitely many algebra generators $c_1,\ldots,c_r$.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof, from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U.

proof.text: Lift each $c_j$ through $q$ and express its lift as a finite sum $\sum_k b_{jk}\otimes b\prime_{jk}$. Collect the finitely many second entries $b\prime_{jk}$ into a list $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ in $B$. Then $c_j=\sum_k t(b_{jk})s(b\prime_{jk})$, so every $c_j$ lies in the $t(B)$-subalgebra generated by the $s(g_i)$. As the $c_j$ generate $C$, so do the $s(g_i)$. An empty list is allowed, in particular if $C$ is already generated by its coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof, from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U.

proof.text: Each $g\in B$ gives a global section of $\mathcal F$: in every chart diagram of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], pull back $g$ along the chart map to the source $U$; these sections commute with all chart restrictions, hence define the required cones and compatible sections on $X$. Conversely the identity chart of $U$ recovers $g$ from such a global family, giving $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=B$. The free-algebra property in the statement defines $e:\mathcal P=\mathcal O_X[z_1,\ldots,z_m]\to\mathcal F$. By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], its restriction to $U_0$ has target $(p_0)_*\mathcal O_R$ and sends $z_i$ to $s(g_i)$: the section comes from $U_1$, so it pulls back along $p_1$. For any affine etale scheme $T=\operatorname{Spec}D\to U_0$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $T\times_XU_1=R\times_{U_0}T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{B,t}D)$. The section formula in the restriction node identifies $\mathcal F(T)$ with this ring. Each element is a finite sum of $c\otimes d$. Expressing $c$ as a polynomial in the $s(g_i)$ over $t(B)$ rewrites it as a polynomial in $s(g_i)\otimes1$ over $D$. This polynomial gives a section of $\mathcal P(T)$ (coefficients in $\mathcal O_X(T)=D$ and the specified global variables), whose image is the given section. Thus $e(T)$ is surjective on these tests; no claim that arbitrary sheaf sections are globally pure tensors is needed.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof, from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U.

proof.text: For any scheme object $W\to X$ of the small etale site, [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives the surjective etale scheme cover $W\times_XU_0\to W$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to cover its source by affine open schemes $T_a$. The projections $T_a\to U_0$ are etale: both projections of the fibre product are etale, and the open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Thus these are tests from step 5. More formally, the base-change and composition assertions of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] give both this etaleness and the composite covering family $\{T_a\to W\}$. Every section of $\mathcal F(W)$ consequently lifts through $e$ on that cover. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], $e$ is surjective as a map of sheaves. It is also surjective as a map of algebra sheaves: two algebra maps agreeing after $e$ agree locally on these lifts, and therefore agree by the sheaf condition.

source.place: Tag 07V6 (proposition-vanishing-affine), proof, from the choice of U through the surjectivity checked on U.

proof.text: The structure module $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent by its free presentation in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. The polynomial algebra $\mathcal P$, as a module, is the small direct sum of one copy of $\mathcal O_X$ for each monomial, exactly as specified in the statement. The direct-sum assertion of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits] makes $\mathcal P$ quasi-coherent. Its target $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by step 2. Apply the kernel assertion of that same node to the underlying module map of $e$ to obtain the required quasi-coherent kernel. No cohomology vanishing has been used.
